parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  A great oral presentation has three qualities: CLARITY (the audience can understand you), CONFIDENCE (you believe in your content), and CONNECTION (you engage with your audience).
content: 📖 A great oral presentation has three qualities: CLARITY (the audience can understand you), CONFIDENCE (you believe in your content), and CONNECTION (you engage with your audience).

The structure of a 10-minute research presentation follows these sections: OPENING (1-2 min) — greet the audience, introduce yourself and your topic, give a hook. OVERVIEW (30 sec) — tell the audience what you will cover: 'Today I will present...'. BODY (5-6 min) — present your key findings, one sub-question at a time, using your visual aids. DATA SECTION (1 min) — explain your chart or graph. CONCLUSION (1 min) — summarize findings and state your thesis answer. Q&A (2 min) — answer questions from the audience.

The most important presentation skills are: SIGNPOSTING (telling the audience where you are in the presentation), maintaining EYE CONTACT (look at the audience, not your notes), speaking at an appropriate PACE (not too fast), and using GESTURES to emphasize key points.
